issues.title: Dev-mode `stop` leaves the workspace's Browser4 Chrome running

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
cd D:/workspace/Browser4/Browser4-4.14-feat
./b4w.ps1 open --headless https://example.com
# Get-BrowserFootprint -> Browser4Roots = 1 (e.g. chrome PID 251688)
./b4w.ps1 stop
# Get-BrowserFootprint -> Browser4Roots = 1 and Get-Process -Id 251688 -> ALIVE
# Same with the MCP opt-in backend: chrome PID 249556 survived `stop` of java PID 160260.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: `stop` shuts the backend down and closes the browsers that backend launched, so Browser4Roots returns to the pre-open value (the scenario's step 11/12 cleanup expects exactly this).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The Java backend process is stopped, but the Chrome root it launched (and all renderer children) keeps running; the browser's parent PID is the dead backend. Only `close-all` before `stop` avoids the leak. Two orphaned Chrome trees (PIDs 249556, 251688) had to be killed manually with taskkill /T /F.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: In development mode handle_stop() calls stop_workspace_servers_forcibly() (main.rs:27098), which calls shutdown_managed_server_processes_on_port(force=true, ...) (managed_processes.rs:976) and therefore force_stop(pid) = `Stop-Process -Force` / SIGKILL (managed_processes.rs:1420-1442). The JVM is terminated without running shutdown hooks, and stop_workspace_servers_forcibly explicitly 'deliberately skips the global browser sweep' (managed_processes.rs:960-962). The production path (stop_browser4_server_forcibly) does notify close-all and kill_all_browsers; dev mode has no equivalent for the stopped backend's own browsers. The browser is identifiable via the session's <contextDir>/launcher.pid (BrowserProcessReaper).

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/managed_processes.rs:stop_workspace_servers_forcibly() (line 963) and cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_stop() (line 27084)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- In the dev stop path, close the sessions/browsers belonging to each managed port before force-killing the JVM (reuse notify_close_all_sessions_before_force_stop) or terminate the Chrome trees whose parent is the backend being stopped.
- Reuse BrowserProcessReaper.terminate(contextDir) / kill_all_browsers scoped to the workspace registry instead of skipping the browser sweep entirely.
- Add an integration test: open -> stop (without close-all) -> assert zero PULSAR_CHROME roots and exit code 0.
- Make the help text say `close-all` is required before `stop` if browsers must be closed (see issue 3).

issues.title: Two backends on one machine share the DEFAULT browser and session UUID despite an isolated state dir

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
cd D:/workspace/Browser4/Browser4-4.14-feat
./b4w.ps1 open --headless https://example.com                    # backend A on :8282
BROWSER4_CLI_STATE_DIR=$(cygpath -w "$TEMP/b4-isolation") ./b4w.ps1 open --headless https://example.com   # backend B on :8283
# Get-BrowserFootprint -> Browser4Roots stays 1, not 2
# Backend B log: 'Found valid existing Chrome process on port: 20326' / 'Reusing existing Chrome process' / 'Found existing Chrome process on port: 20326 for userDataDir: ...\browser4-pereg\context\groups\default\PULSAR_CHROME\cx.001'
# Both backends report the same session UUID d7ab81a7-...; backend A's tab-list goes from 1 to 2 tabs and the extra tab survives backend B's close-all.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: An isolated state directory yields an isolated backend: its own browser, its own session identity and no effect on the first workspace. In the MCP opt-in variant the footprint should grow by two (own session browser + MCP browser) as the scenario specifies.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Backend B attached to backend A's Chrome (A's PID 227260 owns the reused CDP port 20326; A's java process is its parent), added a tab to A's browser, and reused A's DEFAULT session UUID. The MCP opt-in run likewise increased Browser4Roots by only 1 (main browser + MCP browser) instead of the expected 2, because B's session browser was never launched. development-mode.md claims 'the default browser.profile.mode=DEFAULT profile is per workspace here' and 'Session browser profiles are never shared' — the observed behaviour contradicts both.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The DEFAULT-profile browser context directory is built on a per-user shared base, %TEMP%\browser4-<user>\context\groups\<group>\PULSAR_CHROME\cx.<n> (AppPaths.CONTEXT_BASE_DIR / AppPaths.getContextBaseDir; see PulsarSessionManager.kt:1766 and SessionProfileReaper.kt:144), which is not scoped by -Dapp.data.dir or BROWSER4_CLI_STATE_DIR. ChromeLauncher discovers the already-running Chrome bound to that userDataDir/CDP port and reuses it without checking which backend launched it. In addition, the display-name -> UUID registry is hardcoded to ~/.browser4/session-registry.json (CommandServiceConfig.kt:19), so both backends resolve DEFAULT to the same UUID.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/session/PulsarSessionManager.kt (profile/context-dir resolution, ~line 1700-1766); browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/config/CommandServiceConfig.kt:19; ChromeLauncher reuse lives in the ai.platon.pulsar.chrome dependency ('Found existing Chrome process ... for userDataDir')

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Scope the browser context base directory to the workspace/app-data root (or honor BROWSER4_CLI_STATE_DIR) so context/groups is per backend.
- Before reusing an existing Chrome, verify ownership (a backend/workspace marker in the context dir or the launcher.pid's parent) and refuse to attach to another backend's browser.
- Scope the session display-name registry to the workspace or include the workspace in the key.
- Update development-mode.md and add a regression test that starts two backends concurrently and asserts two distinct browsers, distinct session IDs and no tab leakage.

issues.title: `stop` help says 'Gracefully stop' but dev mode force-kills the backend

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 help   # lists: stop  Gracefully stop the Browser4 server
./b4w.ps1 open --headless https://example.com
./b4w.ps1 stop   # backend dies via Stop-Process -Force, browser left running

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The documented behaviour ('gracefully') matches what happens: sessions are notified, browsers close, the server exits cleanly.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: In development mode handle_stop() calls stop_workspace_servers_forcibly(), which uses force=true (Stop-Process -Force) and skips the browser sweep; no graceful close-all notification is sent, and browsers can be left orphaned. Only the production path performs the graceful notification.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The `stop` description was not updated when dev-mode stop was changed to the force-only workspace-scoped path (commit 3d6d983294 'isolate development-mode backends per checkout').

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_stop() (line 27084) and the `stop` help entry in the command reference

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Change the description to something like: 'Stop the Browser4 server (development mode force-stops this checkout's backend; run close-all first to close its browsers)'.
- Or make dev-mode stop perform the same graceful close-all notification before the forced kill.
- Document the close-all-before-stop requirement in the sessions/development-mode docs.

issues.title: Backend server log location is inconsistently documented and `doctor log` needs a running server

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Read skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md line 340 ('the backend writes its logs inside the runtime bundle') and skills/browser4-cli/references/development-mode.md line 23 ('logs' under <state dir>/app-data/). The actual server log is %TEMP%\browser4\browser4-cli\tmp\cli\browser4-server-jar-port8282-*.log; <state dir>/app-data/logs contains only agent/. Then run ./b4w.ps1 doctor log with the backend stopped.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: One accurate documented location for the dev backend log, or `doctor log` lists the local launcher logs (and prints the directory) even when the backend is down.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Two docs disagree and neither names the directory used in this build; `doctor log` prints '(server not running or log listing unavailable: HTTP request failed ... /api/doctor/log-files)' and exits 0 with no path hint, so a first-time user cannot find the log after a failed start.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The launcher/Spring output is written by the CLI/daemon to %TEMP%\browser4\browser4-cli\tmp\cli\, while SKILL.md and development-mode.md describe the backend's own logging locations. `doctor log` is implemented purely as a backend HTTP call (GET /api/doctor/log-files) with no local fallback.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md line 340; skills/browser4-cli/references/development-mode.md line 23; CLI `doctor log` handler in cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (fetches /api/doctor/log-files)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Document the dev launcher log directory (%TEMP%\browser4\browser4-cli\tmp\cli\) and the production BROWSER4_SERVER_LOG_DIR default in both docs.
- Make `doctor log` fall back to listing local launcher logs when the backend is down, and print the directory it searched.
- Exit non-zero (or clearly mark the output as unavailable) when the log listing cannot be produced.
